claims.text: The standard-power process using 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock does not achieve the required bond-coat thickness.
The baseline process maintains minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Increasing spray-torch power increases the thermal energy received by FeCoNiCrAl particles in flight.
The increased in-flight thermal energy produces a more fully molten particle state before impact.
More complete particle melting improves splat formation.
Improved particle melting and splat formation increase deposition efficiency.
A more fully molten particle state improves adhesion upon impact with the substrate.
A more fully molten particle state improves cohesion within the deposited coating.
Higher deposition efficiency increases coating build-up and bond-coat thickness.
Increasing torch power will produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than the lower-power baseline using the same 15–45 μm feedstock.
Increasing torch power will yield a denser coating.
The higher-power coating will preserve coating integrity relative to the baseline.
An inert or hydrogen-modified gas environment will curb excessive oxidation during higher-power spraying.
The higher-power process will preserve low as-sprayed oxidation.

The intervention remains valid for thermal-spray processes applicable to high-entropy-alloy bond coats under thermal-barrier-coating service conditions, provided it does not induce defects or uncontrolled oxidation.
